solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Area partly covered by London legislation to the west? (5)

annotation.definition: Area partly covered by London legislation to the west?

indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: SE, the South East, a region that takes in part of London

annotation.surface: A question about which lands to the west are subject to laws made in London.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: Wales lies west of London and only some of its laws are made at Westminster, the rest being devolved to its own parliament.
annotation.definitionFit: Wales is a region west of London where Westminster legislation applies only in part.

entries.clue: Suspect Bard wore every costume (8)

indicatorNotes.Suspect: suspect as an adjective means not to be trusted, so the letters are not in their proper order

annotation.surface: An accusation that Shakespeare dressed up in every outfit going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb in a whodunnit about the Bard; it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre's wardrobe is its entire stock of costumes.

entries.clue: Enter details of account’s brand name (3,2)

blocks.note: a logo is a brand's emblem

annotation.surface: Filling in a form with the trading name of a business account.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'account': to log on is to enter your account details. The 's stands for 'has'.
annotation.definitionFit: Logging on means typing in the username and password for your account.

entries.clue: Drunk now, like it or not (2,5)

blocks.note: here = now, as in 'the moment is here'

annotation.surface: Someone announcing they are drunk, and you can take it or leave it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun: a drunk, a SOT.
annotation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is said to close an argument, meaning you will have to accept it whether you like it or not.

entries.clue: Poorly rated deputy ready to be fired (8)

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute or deputy
a primed gun is ready to fire

annotation.surface: A deputy with bad reviews who is about to get the sack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests dismissal from a job; it is the gun sense, where priming comes before firing.
annotation.definitionFit: Subprime loans or borrowers have a poor credit rating.

entries.clue: From attempt to catch salmon, maybe bears suffer cold (11)

indicatorNotes.bears: in a down clue, the part that bears another sits beneath it, so OF FISH goes under STAND

blocks.note: of = from, as in 'a man of Kent'
to fish is to try to catch fish, salmon being one

annotation.surface: Bears catching salmon, and suffering in the cold.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a wildlife scene with bears fishing; 'bears' is only placing one piece under another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an aloof manner: someone who keeps others at arm's length is cold in the social sense.

entries.clue: Later acquisition noted by auditor (3)

indicatorNotes.noted by auditor: an auditor is a listener, so this is what the ear takes in

blocks.note: a buy is a purchase, an acquisition

annotation.surface: An accountant spotting a purchase made after the books closed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' pretends to be an accountant; here it is simply a listener. 'Later' is the casual goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Later!' and 'bye!' are both casual ways of saying goodbye.

entries.clue: Funny comic perhaps uncovered her ferret (7)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: her with its outer letters stripped off

blocks.note: a comic is one kind of magazine, or mag
HER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A strange tale of a comedian meddling with a woman's pet ferret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ferret' is the verb, to hunt about, not the animal; 'comic' is a paper, not a comedian.
annotation.definitionFit: To ferret about is to rummage, searching through things.

entries.clue: Male genes modified to limit alpha element (9)

indicatorNotes.modified: changed, so the letters of genes are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to limit: the rearranged genes enclose the A, keeping it within bounds

blocks.note: rearranged to go round the A
alpha is A in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Genetic engineering on men to restrict some alpha element in them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Male' supplies MAN, not just M, and the rearranged GENES take the A inside: G(A)NESE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this metal, number 25 in the periodic table, is one of the chemical elements.

entries.clue: Broad spiral rotating part of every galaxy (4)

indicatorNotes.rotating: turning round, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a piece of the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of every and the start of galaxy

annotation.surface: A description of a spiral galaxy wheeling around.
annotation.walkthrough: The astronomy is all surface; the answer sits backwards across 'every galaxy'.
annotation.definitionFit: A gyre is a large spiral or circular motion, like an ocean gyre.

entries.clue: Leaders muddled in battle rush order to reorient troops (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Leaders muddled: the first letters of the two words get swapped

blocks.note: fight = battle; it takes the R from the second word
race = rush; it takes the F from the first word

annotation.surface: Confused officers rushing into battle and barking orders to turn the troops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like army commanders; it means the front letters of the words.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Right face!' is the drill command to turn ninety degrees to the right.

entries.clue: Lolly somebody coated with crumbs! (5)

indicatorNotes.coated with: one word covers the other on the outside

blocks.note: crumbs! and my! are both mild exclamations

annotation.surface: An ice lolly dropped and covered in crumbs.
annotation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money, and also an ice lolly, which is where the crumbs come from.
annotation.definitionFit: Lolly is informal British slang for money.

entries.clue: Nothing left of citrus drops, everything sold (5)

indicatorNotes.drops: the citrus fruit lets go of a letter

blocks.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
O (nothing) at the left end is removed

annotation.surface: A market stall down to its last citrus fruit after selling out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Citrus drops' sounds like boiled sweets; it is the orange losing its O.
annotation.definitionFit: A shop's range is its whole selection of goods for sale.

entries.clue: See one box splits quite apart (9)

indicatorNotes.splits: the inserted letters break DATE in two

blocks.note: to see someone is to date them

annotation.surface: A single box being split wide open.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is the romantic sense, going out with someone, and 'splits' puts the other two pieces inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Disparate things are wholly different, quite apart from each other.

entries.clue: Exchange of shots after sit-ins exploited by the left (11)

indicatorNotes.exploited: used for another purpose, so the letters are reworked
indicatorNotes.after: the rally comes after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a rally is an exchange of shots in tennis

annotation.surface: Violence breaking out after left-wing protesters staged sit-ins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exchange of shots' suggests gunfire; it is a tennis rally. 'The left' feels political but is just the side.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinistrally means on or towards the left, from Latin sinister, left.

entries.clue: Bachelor say, if gender reassigned, probably missing balls? (14)

indicatorNotes.reassigned: the letters are given new places

annotation.surface: A crude joke about a bachelor who has changed gender and so lacks certain body parts.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's balls are anatomical; the definition's balls are the ones a clumsy fielder fails to catch.
annotation.definitionFit: A butterfingered person tends to drop things, so is likely to miss catches.

entries.clue: Decent plain rounds within compass of bell-ringer, nearly (9)

indicatorNotes.rounds: turns round, so BARE runs backwards
indicatorNotes.within compass of: inside the bounds of the next word

blocks.note: TOLLER, one who tolls a bell, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A modest description of the plain rounds that bell-ringers chime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' and 'rounds' are both change-ringing terms, which is the disguise: plain here is simply bare, and rounds tells you to turn it round.
annotation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable, decent enough.

entries.clue: A certain stage not available to North Hollywood resident? (8)

indicatorNotes.North: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards

blocks.note: one = a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

annotation.surface: A question about a theatre stage off limits to someone in North Hollywood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North Hollywood' reads as the Los Angeles district, but North is the reversal instruction. The question mark flags that Hollywood is only one example of Los Angeles.
annotation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native or resident of Los Angeles, which includes Hollywood.

entries.clue: Grafter losing in photo finish for medals, pressure showing (7,7)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the word for losing goes within the word for photo
indicatorNotes.finish for: the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: a film that's on is showing

annotation.surface: An athlete who worked hard losing a photo finish for medals under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grafter' looks like a hard worker, but it is someone who grafts skin. 'Photo finish' is not a phrase here: 'losing' is split off and slipped inside the photo.
annotation.definitionFit: A plastic surgeon performs skin grafts.

entries.clue: Posers which may only trouble the 14 across? (7)

annotation.definition2: which may only trouble the 14 across?

blocks.note: a sitter poses for a portrait

blocks.clueFragment: which may only trouble the 14 across?
blocks.note: a sitter is an easy catch that only a butterfingered fielder would drop

annotation.surface: Awkward problems that bother only the clumsy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posers' suggests puzzles; it is models. In cricket a sitter is a catch so easy that only a butterfingered player would miss it.
annotation.definitionFit: Sitters pose for artists, and in cricket a sitter is a dolly catch.

entries.clue: Come back to minister — can that be true? (7)

annotation.surface: Someone doubting news about a minister's return.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minister' tempts toward politics; it is the clergy sense, giving REV.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: returning to a place or topic you have been to before.

entries.clue: Famous printmaker saving a frame for painting (9)

indicatorNotes.saving: save = except, so A is left out

annotation.surface: A celebrated engraver keeping a frame for a painting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving' seems to mean keeping; it means except, as in 'all save one'.
annotation.definitionFit: A stretcher is the wooden frame a painting's canvas is stretched over.

entries.clue: Certain that charges impress a felon (4)

indicatorNotes.charges: to charge is to load, so these words hold the answer

annotation.surface: Criminal charges designed to make an impression on a lawbreaker.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface hides the answer across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'a safe bet', one sure to come off.

entries.clue: Woolly you finally gave back after cycling (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of you is used
indicatorNotes.back: giving something back returns it the way it came, so gave is read in reverse
indicatorNotes.after cycling: then letters move round from the front to the back

annotation.surface: A complaint that after a bike ride you handed back something woolly.
annotation.walkthrough: U plus EVAG makes UEVAG; move the first two letters to the end and it becomes VAGUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Woolly is an idiom for fuzzy, muddled thinking that lacks a clear outline.

entries.clue: Dark room with throne beneath Grand Mughal’s crown (5)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, LOO goes under G
indicatorNotes.crown: the top, so the first letter

blocks.note: the throne is a jokey word for the toilet

annotation.surface: A gloomy chamber housing the throne of a great Mughal emperor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dark room' looks like a photographer's darkroom; the definition is just 'Dark', and the room with a throne is a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Dark as a noun, the absence of light; the answer is partial darkness.

entries.clue: Lie on thin bit of fabric (5)

annotation.surface: Lying down on a scrap of cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie' reads as reclining; it is the untruth.
annotation.definitionFit: Cloth is woven from threads, each spun from fine strands: those are the thin bits.

entries.clue: Heavy load troubles European on motorway going around 100 mph (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after M
indicatorNotes.going around: to go around something is to encircle it, so ILLS and E wrap round TON

blocks.note: doing a ton is driving at 100 mph

annotation.surface: A heavy lorry in trouble as a European driver speeds down the motorway at 100 mph.
annotation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on, hence M; a ton is slang for 100 mph.
annotation.definitionFit: A millstone round your neck is a heavy burden.

entries.clue: Structure resisting great pressure from below cracked (3)

indicatorNotes.from below: in a down clue, read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a dam holds back the weight of water

annotation.surface: An engineering note about a structure giving way under pressure from beneath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' fits the engineering picture of a failing dam; it is the definition, meaning crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Cracked is informal slang for crazy, the mind likened to a broken pot.

entries.clue: Revised dates agreed after loud festival (5,3)

indicatorNotes.Revised: changed, so the letters of dates are rearranged

annotation.surface: Organisers agreeing new dates for a noisy festival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud festival' feels like one phrase; loud gives F and festival is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a saint's day or holy day in the church calendar, marked by celebration.

entries.clue: Rate model making late start in occupation (5)

indicatorNotes.making: late is exchanged for another letter

blocks.note: a template is a model to copy
first letter of occupation, put in LATE's place

annotation.surface: A price quoted for a model who is late starting a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making late start' looks like a tardy beginning; LATE in TEMPLATE is replaced by O.
annotation.definitionFit: Tempo is rate or speed, especially of music.
